# plan-if-needed overwrites operator-confirmed effort/risk

Discovered-from: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 (plan session 2026-10-27).

## Problem

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` `plan-if-needed` re-runs the effort-and-risk
estimator whenever no prior `effort_and_risk_skill` comment exists on the item
(`is_effort_risk_computed`), silently overwriting operator-confirmed
effort/risk values with heuristic estimates. On SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 the
operator-confirmed carry-over risk High / effort M was replaced with Extra
Small / Low (comment 09:38:39Z), materially understating risk of a commit-gate
change. The original values were restored manually.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan-if-needed` never overwrites an explicitly set/human-confirmed
      effort or risk with a heuristic recomputation; the recompute path is gated
      on the absence of a deliberate value (with a recorded rationale), or the
      overwrite is surfaced as an explicit warning/approval.
- [ ] A regression test covers the overwrite scenario (operator value present,
      no prior estimator comment) and asserts the value is preserved.
- [ ] Origin case documented: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 restore comment
      SA-C0MVQKM7XD0089OVQ.
data.title: plan-if-needed overwrites operator-confirmed effort/risk

Discovered during LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 (llm worklog) via test-failure SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ.

## Problem
`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` and exercises the real `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, which imports `numpy` (line 117). The repo declares no Python dependency manifest (no `requirements.txt`), so on a bare interpreter the whole unit node suite fails with `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` — the failure was red on this host from 2026-10-15 until numpy was installed ad hoc during the item above.

## Goal
As a maintainer, I want the voice-input worker's Python dependencies declared (and/or the unit test to skip with a clear message when they are absent), so a fresh checkout's full suite is green without undocumented host setup.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The worker's Python runtime dependencies (numpy, faster-whisper) are declared in a committed manifest (e.g. `pi-client/voice-input/requirements.txt`) and referenced from the voice-input README setup table.
2. `tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` either documents the install step in its header or skips (with an explicit, non-silent message) when the resolved interpreter cannot import the required modules.
3. Full suite is green on an interpreter provisioned only from the committed manifest (verified via the test skill; no ad-hoc pip installs).

## Out of scope
Changing the worker's transcription behaviour or its stub-based test contract.

## Related
- SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ — the test-failure item that surfaced this.
- LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 — llm worklog item whose dev-push gate was blocked by it (code in SorraAgents).

# Audit F3 execution worktree does not link vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` → spurious test failures and self-blocking triage children

**Discovered from:** WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 (Create a podcast for standups), `/skill:audit` run on 2026-11-21. Companion defect: the cross-repo `--code-root` code-quality scope bug (separate work item).

## Problem statement

The audit's default-on F3 suite execution builds a fresh execution worktree (`<repo>/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-<id>`, and a pinned worktree in the two-stage merge-gate path) and symlinks the **shared root `node_modules`** — but it does not provide the **vendored** dependency trees under `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`. Suites that exercise vendored extensions therefore fail inside the audit worktree while passing in the normal checkout.

Observed in the audit of WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 (ContentCreator suite, HEAD `d250032d4cea1f6a14b57459751eebdce1245acd`):

```
E  AssertionError: The vendored wiki extension is unavailable, so the rebuild cannot run:
   Cannot find package 'mdast-util-from-markdown' imported from
   /home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8/.pi/packages/pi-llm-wiki-manual/...
```

The package **is** present in the normal checkout (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/.pi/packages/pi-llm-wiki-manual/node_modules/mdast-util-from-markdown`), so the failure is an artefact of the audit worktree, not of the audited code. Three tests in `tests/test_rebuild_wiki_meta.py` failed this way.

## Consequence (why this is high priority)

1. The failures were correctly classified `unit`/`unrelated` and **excused** under the permissive test-failure mode — but they are still triaged, and triage created a **high-priority `test-failure` child parented to the audited epic** (`WL-0MWQXIR2J0001E1A`).
2. That child's own AC ("the test passes against the latest `dev`") is `unmet`, so the parent's audit verdict became **`Ready to close: No`** and the item was flagged `needsProducerReview` — an otherwise fully-complete epic blocked by a dependency artefact of the audit harness itself.
3. The producer had to review and delete the child as spurious before the item could be re-audited.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The audit F3 execution worktree (single-stage and the two-stage pinned/merge-gate variant) provides **every** vendored dependency tree the suite needs — e.g. initialise submodules, then link or bootstrap both the root `node_modules` **and** each `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` (or run the project's own bootstrap/install step).
- [ ] A repo whose suite depends on a vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` yields the **same** suite verdict in the audit execution worktree as in the normal checkout at the same commit.
- [ ] Suite failures whose evidence is a missing/absent dependency inside the audit worktree are classified as **infrastructure**, not product failures: they never create `test-failure` work items and never leave the audited item blocked by an auto-created child.
- [ ] A regression test pins the worktree preparation (or the infra-failure classification) without requiring a real suite run.
- [ ] `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` records the worktree dependency provisioning contract next to the existing `node_modules` symlink conventions.

## Impact

Audits stop failing work that is actually finished: vendored-dependency tests behave identically in the audit worktree and the real checkout, so no spurious high-priority test-failure child is created and producers are not asked to review and delete phantom blockers.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — F3 execution-worktree creation / `node_modules` symlink path, and the test-failure triage hand-off.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — suite execution in a supplied worktree (`cwd=`), triage classification of failures.
- `skill/triage/` — the `test-failure` item creation path (evidence used to decide whether a failure is infrastructure).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — worktree provision / symlink conventions.

## Evidence / related

- Logs: `~/.audit_debug/ContextHub/audit_run_WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8_20261121T213400.log`, `..._20261121T215624_rerun.log`.
- Deleted spurious child (recorded for traceability): `WL-0MWQXIR2J0001E1A` (ContextHub worklog, parented to `WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8`, deleted by the producer on 2026-11-21).
- Related existing conventions: `node_modules` symlink into audit worktrees (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ, SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B, SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B** – Auto-symlink node_modules into implement worktrees (implement.py start) (completed)
- **SA-0MSHZ08OY005EE7W** – Delete AMPA installer/plugin test artifacts (completed)
- **SA-0MSF8KNE3003JDVD** – Fix node --test directory invocation in test skill runner (node v22 treats dirs as modules) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0msgs763c006sm1b, 0msn52ggn002b0az, 0mvtor53e003iieq, absent, acceptance (+177 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0msgs763c006sm1b, 0msn52ggn002b0az, absent, acceptance, actually (+176 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0msgs763c006sm1b, absent, acceptance, actually, artefact (+175 more)

# Pin audit-worktree vendored dependency parity with a regression fixture

**Parent:** SA-0MWQZGZ83001RSO6 (Audit F3 execution worktree misses vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`)

Verification slice — created first (test-first ordering), executed after the two
implementation slices it exercises (dependency edges below).

## Goal

Pin the parent item's parity and regression-test criteria with an offline fixture,
and record the real-content parity evidence from the observed incident, so the
defect cannot silently return.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Covers parent AC2 — A repo whose suite depends on a vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` yields the **same** suite verdict in the audit execution worktree as in the normal checkout at the same commit.
- [ ] Covers parent AC4 — A regression test pins the worktree preparation (or the infra-failure classification) without requiring a real suite run.
- [ ] An offline `tmp_path` fixture builds a repo with a tracked `.pi/packages/<pkg>` whose dependency lives in a gitignored `.pi/packages/<pkg>/node_modules/<dep>`; the tests assert both the F3 execution worktree and the merge-gate worktree resolve `<dep>` from inside the worktree after provisioning.
- [ ] The same fixture pins the incident record shape at the triage boundary: an infrastructure-evidence failure produces zero `test-failure` children and no dependency edge on the audited parent, asserted through the production classifier and triage helper without executing a real suite.
- [ ] Parity evidence is recorded in the completion comment: the three failing ContentCreator tests (`tests/test_rebuild_wiki_meta.py`, commit `d250032d4cea1f6a14b57459751eebdce1245acd`) pass under an audit execution worktree, or the residual difference and its cause are documented.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/` with a vendored-package repo builder: a bare remote plus a clone whose tracked `.pi/packages/<pkg>/package.json` requires `<dep>`, with `<dep>` materialised only in the clone's `.pi/packages/<pkg>/node_modules/` (gitignored), mirroring ContentCreator.
2. `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_worktree_dependencies.py` — drive the real `_create_execution_worktree` and `_integrate_into_dev` helpers with the fake-runner pattern from `test_audit_runner_execution_worktree_host.py`, then assert `<dep>` resolves from inside each worktree (directory/`require.resolve` check — no suite execution).
3. Assert the suppression path end-to-end at the record level: infrastructure evidence → no `check_or_create` call, no `wl` mutation.
4. Run the ContentCreator reproduction (audit `WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8` shape, same commit) and record the result in the completion comment.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/vendored_node_modules_repo.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_worktree_dependencies.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_execution_worktree_host.py` (pattern to mirror)

## Constraints

- Offline, `tmp_path`-only: no network, no `npm install`, no real suite execution (parent AC4).
- Written red-first inside this slice — the repo forbids committing a red tree, so the failing assertions land with the provisioning/classification slices they verify.

## Impact

The audit's vendored-dependency behaviour is pinned by an offline regression test, so a future change to worktree preparation fails the suite instead of silently re-introducing phantom audit failures.
data.title: Pin audit-worktree vendored dependency parity with a regression fixture

# Provision vendored `node_modules` in audit worktrees

**Parent:** SA-0MWQZGZ83001RSO6 (Audit F3 execution worktree misses vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`)

## Problem

The audit creates two throwaway worktrees — the F3 **execution** worktree
(`<host>/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-<id>`, `_create_execution_worktree`) and the
merge-gate **integration** worktree (`audit-merge-<id>`, `_integrate_into_dev`).
Both initialise git submodules and symlink the **root** `node_modules` only. A repo
that vendors a pi package under `.pi/packages/<pkg>/` with its own gitignored
`node_modules` therefore has an unresolvable dependency graph inside the worktree
while the populated checkout resolves it fine (observed: ContentCreator
`tests/test_rebuild_wiki_meta.py`, `Cannot find package 'mdast-util-from-markdown'`).

`implement.py` already solves this for implement worktrees
(`_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`). The audit has no equivalent, and there
must be **one** provisioner, not a second copy.

## Scope

- Promote the nested-`node_modules` discovery + symlink logic into a shared module.
- Call it from both audit worktree creation sites, after submodule initialisation
  and before the build/suite runs.
- Emit evidence lines so a reviewer can see what was provisioned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Covers parent AC1 — The audit F3 execution worktree (single-stage and the two-stage pinned/merge-gate variant) provides **every** vendored dependency tree the suite needs — e.g. initialise submodules, then link or bootstrap both the root `node_modules` **and** each `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` (or run the project's own bootstrap/install step).
- [ ] One shared provisioner (`skill/shared/worktree_deps.py`) discovers nested `node_modules` directories under a checkout root and symlinks each into the worktree, never overwriting an existing entry and never fabricating a package directory the worktree lacks.
- [ ] `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` keeps `_iter_nested_node_modules` / `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` as delegating wrappers, so its existing call sites and patched tests are unchanged.
- [ ] Both `_create_execution_worktree` (F3 execution worktree) and `_integrate_into_dev` (merge-gate worktree) provision nested `node_modules` after `_ensure_worktree_submodules` and before the build/suite, appending greppable evidence (`nested node_modules provisioned: <n> (<paths>)`, or a best-effort failure note).
- [ ] Provisioning is best-effort: a failure records evidence and never aborts the audit or fails the merge gate.
- [ ] Unit tests in `skill/shared/tests/test_worktree_deps.py` cover discovery pruning (`.git`/`.worklog`/`node_modules` never descended, symlinked dirs never followed, root `node_modules` excluded), symlink creation, no-overwrite, missing-parent skip, and per-candidate failure tolerance — with no suite execution.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Move `_NESTED_NODE_MODULES_PRUNE_DIRS`, `_iter_nested_node_modules` and `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` into `skill/shared/worktree_deps.py` (public names `iter_nested_node_modules`, `ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`).
2. Re-export them from `implement.py` as thin wrappers preserving the current return types and log lines.
3. Add `_provision_worktree_dependencies(worktree_path, host_root) -> list[str]` in `audit_runner.py`: the existing root `node_modules` symlink plus the nested symlinks, returning evidence lines.
4. Call it from `_create_execution_worktree` (after submodules, replacing the inline symlink block) and from `_integrate_into_dev` (same point in the integration sequence).
5. Add `skill/shared/tests/test_worktree_deps.py` — written red-first.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/worktree_deps.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_worktree_deps.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` (existing merge-gate coverage to extend)

## Constraints

- Fail-open, mirroring `_ensure_worktree_submodules`: never a new hard dependency of the audit.
- Symlinks only: never copy, never install, never invoke a package manager inside a worktree (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B convention).
- Preserve the ordering hazard fix: submodules → dependency provisioning → build/suite (SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ).
- Cross-repo `--code-root` hosting of the merge-gate worktree is **out of scope** (execution-worktree hosting was SA-0MWO59J9T002IQ63); this slice provisions from the root each site already uses.

## Impact

Suites in the audit's throwaway worktrees resolve the same dependency graph as the real checkout, so vendored-package tests stop failing for environmental reasons.
data.title: Provision vendored node_modules in audit worktrees

# Classify audit-worktree dependency failures as infrastructure

**Parent:** SA-0MWQZGZ83001RSO6 (Audit F3 execution worktree misses vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`)

## Problem

`_run_tests_via_test_skill` triages every parsed failure **before** the red-suite
mode evaluation runs, so a failure caused by the audit worktree's own missing
dependency still mints a critical `test-failure` child on the audited item
(WL-0MWQXIR2J0001E1A in the observed incident). The consequence: a complete epic
reads "Ready to close: No" and needs producer review to delete a phantom blocker.

A suppression contract already exists for verdicts that must never mint an item —
`detect_phantom` / `PHANTOM_NOTICE_CODES` for `state_changed_during_run`
(WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET). This slice adds the infrastructure case alongside it.

## Scope

- Evidence-based detector: a module-resolution failure whose importer path resolves
  inside the audit execution worktree **and** whose named dependency exists in the
  populated checkout.
- Audit runner: suppress those failures from triage (before any `wl` mutation) and
  report them.
- Triage helper: honour an explicit infrastructure signal so no caller can mint an
  item from it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Covers parent AC3 — Suite failures whose evidence is a missing/absent dependency inside the audit worktree are classified as **infrastructure**, not product failures: they never create `test-failure` work items and never leave the audited item blocked by an auto-created child.
- [ ] Detection is conservative and evidence-based: a missing-module/package failure is infrastructure only when the failing importer path resolves inside the audit execution worktree AND the named dependency is present in the populated checkout; a genuinely missing product dependency stays a product failure.
- [ ] The audit runner skips triage for infrastructure failures before any `wl` mutation (no `check_or_create` call, no dependency wiring) and records them in a `suppressed_infrastructure` result key plus the run summary line and gate evidence.
- [ ] `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` suppresses on the explicit signal (`notice_code: missing_dependency_in_worktree` or `infrastructure: true`) exactly as it does for phantoms, returning `suppressed: true` without a lookup or creation.
- [ ] Infrastructure failures never upgrade an execution-dependent AC to `met`: no green evidence means the AC stays `partial` (the runner's fail-closed evidence invariant is preserved).
- [ ] Unit tests pin detection positives and negatives plus both suppression paths (audit runner and triage helper) without executing a suite.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `skill/shared/test_infra.py`: `INFRA_NOTICE_CODE`, `detect_missing_dependency(text)` (Node `Cannot find module/package`, `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, Python `ModuleNotFoundError`, TS2307) and `classify_infrastructure_failure(failure, *, worktree_root, main_checkout_root)` returning `None` unless environment causality is proven.
2. `audit_runner.py`: partition `failures` before the triage loop so only product failures reach `check_or_create`; add `suppressed_infrastructure` to the returned dict and the `Test skill run completed:` summary line; surface the count in the evidence block.
3. `triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`: `detect_infrastructure(payload)` checked after `detect_phantom`, returning the same suppressed shape (no lookup, no creation, no dependency edge).
4. Tests: `skill/shared/tests/test_test_infra.py`, `skill/triage/tests/test_check_or_create_infrastructure.py`, and an audit-runner test asserting zero triage calls for an infrastructure failure record.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/test_infra.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_test_infra.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`
- `skill/triage/tests/test_check_or_create_infrastructure.py` (new)

## Constraints

- No inferred similarity: suppression fires only on evidence proving environment causality, so a genuine failure on a stable checkout is never swallowed.
- Never suppress a failure whose evidence does not name a missing module/package.
- Do not widen this into "excuse every unrelated failure": that ordering question is separate and out of scope.

## Impact

A missing vendored dependency inside the audit worktree can no longer create a phantom high-priority `test-failure` blocker on the audited item.
data.title: Classify audit-worktree dependency failures as infrastructure

# Document the worktree dependency provisioning contract

**Parent:** SA-0MWQZGZ83001RSO6 (Audit F3 execution worktree misses vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`)

## Goal

Record the provisioning contract next to the existing `node_modules` symlink
conventions so the next person changing worktree preparation knows what must be
provisioned, in what order, and how failures are classified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Covers parent AC5 — `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` records the worktree dependency provisioning contract next to the existing `node_modules` symlink conventions.
- [ ] The section states the provisioning order (submodules → root `node_modules` → nested vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` → build/suite), the fail-open semantics, and the exact evidence lines emitted by both worktree kinds.
- [ ] The infrastructure-failure classification contract is documented in the same reference: the evidence required (missing module named by the failure, importer path inside the audit worktree, dependency present in the populated checkout), the suppression behaviour (no `test-failure` item, no dependency edge), and that a suppressed failure never upgrades an AC to `met`.
- [ ] Existing `node_modules` mentions in the reference cross-reference the new subsection instead of restating it.
- [ ] The documented helper and evidence names match the shipped code (no stale anchors or paths).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the subsection under the existing worktree-conventions material (next to the `node_modules` symlink and submodule-ordering notes, around the F3 execution-worktree section).
2. Cross-reference from the merge-gate integration bullet and the F3 execution-worktree bullet.
3. Record the incident shape (ContentCreator `tests/test_rebuild_wiki_meta.py`, WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 / WL-0MWQXIR2J0001E1A) as the rationale, one paragraph.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`

## Impact

The worktree provisioning and infrastructure-classification contracts are written down next to the conventions they extend, so the next change to audit worktree preparation starts from the documented rule instead of rediscovering it via a phantom failure.

Planning Complete (plan skill) — SA-0MWQZGZ83001RSO6

## Decomposition (4 children, dependency order)

| Order | Item | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SA-0MWR3O7RW0009GHT — Provision vendored `node_modules` in audit worktrees | bug | Shared provisioner (`skill/shared/worktree_deps.py`) wired into both audit worktree sites (parent AC1) |
| 2 | SA-0MWR3O8UZ004WF4A — Classify audit-worktree dependency failures as infrastructure | bug | Evidence-based infra classification + triage suppression (parent AC3) |
| 3 | SA-0MWR3O32D0081MUC — Pin audit-worktree vendored dependency parity with a regression fixture | task | Offline regression fixture pinning provisioning + parity + suppression (parent AC2/AC4) |
| 4 | SA-0MWR3O9W50078ETG — Document the worktree dependency provisioning contract | docs | Reference contract next to the symlink conventions (parent AC5) |

Dependency edges: SA-0MWR3O32D0081MUC depends on SA-0MWR3O7RW0009GHT and
SA-0MWR3O8UZ004WF4A; SA-0MWR3O9W50078ETG depends on both as well.

**Test-first ordering.** The verification slice (SA-0MWR3O32D0081MUC) is created
first. It is *executed* after the two implementation slices because the repo
forbids committing a red tree — the failing assertions land inside the slice
they verify (TDD within each child), and the dedicated verification child then
pins the end-to-end contract. AC coverage review: 100 %, recommendation
`proceed`, no auto-created gaps.

## Key findings from the code read (basis for the slices)

1. **Gap confirmed.** `_create_execution_worktree` (`audit_runner.py`) and
   `_integrate_into_dev` each symlink only the *root* `node_modules`; neither
   provisions nested vendored trees. `implement.py` already has
   `_iter_nested_node_modules` / `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`, so the
   fix is extraction + wiring, not new logic.
2. **Root cause of the phantom child is ordering, not only provisioning.**
   `_run_tests_via_test_skill` triages every parsed failure *before*
   `_evaluate_red_suite` decides relatedness, so even an excused failure mints a
   `test-failure` child. The suppression contract to mirror already exists:
   `detect_phantom` / `PHANTOM_NOTICE_CODES` (WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET).
3. **ContentCreator shape verified.** `.pi/packages/pi-llm-wiki-manual/node_modules`
   is gitignored (`ContentCreator/.gitignore:31`) and present only in the main
   checkout — exactly the missing-in-worktree evidence the detector must require.

## Assumptions (documented, no producer input required)

- "Two-stage pinned/merge-gate variant" = the two worktree creation sites in
  `audit_runner.py` (`_create_execution_worktree`, `_integrate_into_dev`). No
  other worktree concept exists in the runner.
- Provisioning is **link-only** (symlinks of what the populated checkout already
  has); no `npm install` inside a worktree, per the SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B convention.
  A dependency absent from the populated checkout is not bootstrapped — the audit
  stays fail-open and the classification requires "present in the checkout".
- An infrastructure failure never upgrades an execution-dependent AC to `met`
  (fail-closed evidence invariant): it suppresses triage and is reported, but
  still yields no green evidence.
- Cross-repo `--code-root` hosting of the *merge-gate* worktree is out of scope
  (execution-worktree hosting was SA-0MWO59J9T002IQ63).
- Broader question "should permissive-mode excused failures be triaged at all?"
  is deliberately out of scope: this item's AC3 is scoped to
  missing-dependency-in-worktree evidence.
